title: dynamic-credit-backpressure-and-kv-inline-prefetch-for-streaming-low-p99
author: Maya Chen
commits: a1f4c2b: initial dynamic credit allocator and scheduler hook
b7d9e3f: inline KV prefetcher + hot-prefix tracking
c3e8a90: metrics, tracing and unit tests for credit model
d2b7411: integration tests and perf bench harness updates
e9c5f77: address review comments, fallback for cold-starts
body:
Summary: Introduce a dynamic credit-based backpressure mechanism for streaming connections plus an inline KV prefetcher that reduces first-token and p99 tail latency for common prefixes.

Motivation: We observed intermittent p99 spikes on hosted streaming when a few connections generated long sequences causing kernel queues and KV miss penalties to cascade. Fixed window throttles (tokens-per-interval) are too coarse and either add latency or drop throughput.

Design: Replace the global fixed flush windows with a per-stream credit allocator. Each active stream receives credits proportional to an adaptive budget computed from: kernel queue length, recent token service time, and observed KV hit-rate. Credits are consumed per-token generation; when credits are low we request rapid async refill or apply lightweight pacing. To address cold-start KV misses, the inline KV prefetcher tracks hot prefixes at scheduler time and performs a non-blocking prefetch into the local KV cache prior to first-token generation for predicted prefixes.

Key behaviors:
- Credit allocator is in runtime/streaming/credit_scheduler.* and exposes a small API for stream_controller to request credits; it uses EWMA of service times and a configurable headroom factor.
- Prefetcher lives in runtime/kv and exposes `prefetch_for_prefix(stream_id, prefix_hash)`; it's non-blocking and has a bounded concurrency counter to avoid overloading the KV backend.
- Scheduler hook (policy_hooks.h) uses kernel queue depth metric to temporarily boost credits for latency-sensitive streams and deprioritize long-batch microjobs.
- Fallbacks: if prefetch fails or KV hit-rate is low, streams fall back to existing async KV fetch path; if credit allocator is disabled via config, behavior reverts to previous fixed-window flush cadence.

Commits & changes: See commits array for high-level commit summary. Files changed include new credit scheduler, inline prefetcher, tests, perf harness, and a small kernel pacing patch to smoother enqueue bursts.

Performance results (bench/perf_stream_latency.py):
- In our internal benchmark with mixed short-chat and long-generation workloads: median first-token latency improved ~18%, p95 improved ~30%, p99 improved ~42% on hosts with heavy contention.
- On dedicated hardware (no KV network), improvements were smaller for median but p99 still ~25% due to reduced kernel queue amplification.

Tests: added unit tests for credit math and concurrency invariants, integration tests for prefetcher correctness and end-to-end perf harness.

CI: initial CI run failed due to a flaky test `credit_model_test::handles_underflow` on macOS builders; fixed by tightening timer stubbing and re-ran CI.

Review discussion (summary):
- Rafiq: asked for observability (per-stream credit metrics, prefetch success/failure counters). Author: added metrics and tracing spans, documented in docs/notes/streaming_credit_design.md.
- Sofia: requested safe opt-out and config knobs for enterprise/private (we added `streaming.credit_allocator.enabled=false` and `kv.inline_prefetch.enabled=false`).
- Theo: flagged potential for KV overfetch at scale; we added bounded concurrent prefetch counters and backoff policy.
- Also discussed how this interacts with existing prefix/KV caching; we added explicit compatibility notes.

Backwards compatibility and rollout: feature is behind two config flags and gateable via rollout service in Redwood Console. Default rollout set to 20% of hosted traffic for 72h with aggressive monitoring (token latency, kernel queue depth, KV QPS).

Release notes: "Streaming: dynamic credit-based backpressure and inline KV prefetch to cut first-byte and p99 token latencies; gated rollout and config tunables."

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: prefetcher could increase KV QPS; mitigation: bounded concurrency and adaptive backoff, and monitored dashboards added.
- Risk: mis-calibrated credits causing starvation; mitigation: headroom defaults conservative and circuit-breaker to revert to fixed window.

Follow-ups:
- Tweak EWMA windows and headroom after 72h ramp (ENG-3229).
- Expand prefetcher heuristics to include recent user prompts and telemetry-driven hot-prefix mining.
- Evaluate moving credit allocator to a centralized heuristic service for cross-host coordination.

Merge: Squash-merged after approvals and green CI.

JIRA/SUPPORT: linked SUP-4421 for customer reports that motivated part of this work.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps algorithm parameters configurable and instruments new metrics to allow iterative tuning in production. Change log and docs updated.
